title: No Host or Origin validation: a DNS-rebinding page gets full same-origin access to the management API and /mcp
what_happens: uvicorn/FastAPI answer any Host header (verified: Host: attacker.example -> 200) and POST /mcp ignores Origin (verified: Origin: http://evil.example -> ping 200). No TrustedHostMiddleware, no CORS layer, no Sec-Fetch-Site or Origin check on any route. After a rebind the attacker's page is same-origin with 192.168.0.180:8000, so JSON POSTs need no preflight and responses are readable. The full rebind race was not executed; both preconditions were verified.
impact: Drive-by from any web page David visits while the service runs: create a tool, run it, read back OMNIFORGE_API_KEY, the SQLite database and every tool's source, all inside the container. No LAN foothold needed. Exposed/tunnelled: critical.
repro: curl -H 'Host: attacker.example' http://127.0.0.1:18307/api/tools -> 200; POST /mcp with Origin: http://evil.example -> 200.
fix: Add Starlette TrustedHostMiddleware with an explicit allow-list (NAS IP/hostname, localhost); reject state-changing requests whose Origin/Sec-Fetch-Site is not same-origin; apply the MCP spec's Origin check on /mcp. Pair with BUG-002 and BUG-006.

title: Body-less POST /api/tools/{name}/run and /toggle are CORS 'simple requests': any web page on the LAN can execute or disable tools
what_happens: Neither route requires a JSON body, a custom header or a same-origin check, so fetch(url,{method:'POST',mode:'no-cors'}) from any origin is sent without preflight. Verified: POST /run with Origin: http://evil.example and Content-Type: text/plain and an empty body -> 200 {"stdout":"executed"}; the same to /toggle -> 200 {"is_active":false}. OPTIONS -> 405 and text/plain create -> 422, so only run/toggle are blind-fireable without rebinding.
impact: Any page opened by any LAN browser can run every saved tool with {} (side effects, network calls, credentials embedded in code) or silently disable tools for AI discovery. Guessable names (the four example tools) make this blind attack practical.
fix: Require Content-Type: application/json plus a custom header (e.g. X-OmniForge: 1) that the dashboard always sends, or check Sec-Fetch-Site/Origin == same-origin, on every POST/PUT/DELETE; reject otherwise with 403.

title: Studio description field is bound to <meta name="description">: typed descriptions are silently discarded and never displayed
what_happens: field('description') = document.querySelector('[name="description"]') matches the <meta name="description"> in <head> (line 7) before #toolDescription. Verified in Chromium: tagName === 'META'. fillEditor and formValues read/write an expando on the meta element, so the textarea is never populated or read, and typing in it does not mark the form dirty.
impact: Every tool authored in the dashboard is saved with description '' (or, after a template, the template's text the user cannot see); editing a description reports 'Tool saved' but keeps the old value; no unsaved-changes prompt. The description is the main signal an LLM uses to choose a tool, so dashboard-made tools are effectively unlabelled in tools/list. The fake-DOM unit tests lack the <meta> tag and cannot catch it.
repro: Open #tools/new, run document.querySelector('[name="description"]').tagName -> 'META'. Type a description, save, GET /api/tools -> description ''.
fix: const field = name => document.getElementById('toolForm').elements[name]; add a real-browser regression that saves a description and reads it back.

title: Tool execution, pip/npm installs and the lock busy-wait run synchronously inside async handlers and freeze the whole server
what_happens: api_run_tool and mcp_endpoint are async def but call run_tool() -> subprocess.run (up to timeout+15 s), ensure_dependencies (pip/npm up to 120 s, flock polling with time.sleep up to 125 s) on the single uvicorn event loop. Verified: two concurrent 3 s runs completed in 3.02 s and 6.04 s (serialised); GET /api/config issued during them took 5.54 s.
impact: While any tool runs, the dashboard, /api/config, every other MCP client's tools/list and tools/call, and any health check stall; clients time out and retry, piling up more blocking work. A first-run install plus a slow script can freeze the service for minutes.
fix: Run the script with asyncio.create_subprocess_exec (or anyio.to_thread.run_sync(run_tool)) and installs in a worker thread; add a per-tool and global semaphore; replace the sleep-poll lock wait. Because runs then overlap, write each run's script to a per-run temp dir (see BUG-015).

title: Scripts inherit the full application environment, including OMNIFORGE_API_KEY, DB and lib paths
what_happens: environment = os.environ.copy() is passed to every script and to every package it imports, while the installer already uses a scrubbed environment. Verified: a tool returned key_present=true, lib_root_present=true. tests/test_dependencies.py asserts the key IS passed, locking the behaviour in.
impact: The only credential in the system is readable by every tool, every dependency and anyone who reaches /run (BUG-001/002/006). Leaked keys flow into LLM transcripts and logs. Prerequisite for any secrets feature.
fix: Build an allow-listed environment (PATH, HOME, LANG, TMPDIR, PYTHONPATH/NODE_PATH, explicit per-tool extras) mirroring _installer_environment(); invert the test to assert the key is absent.

title: Dashboard and management API are unauthenticated: create + run is arbitrary code execution for anyone who reaches the port
what_happens: _check_api_key is referenced only by POST /mcp. GET /, /api/config, GET/POST /api/tools, PUT/DELETE/toggle/run and GET /mcp accept requests with no credential.
impact: Any LAN host, process or malware gets in-container RCE, every tool's source, the DB and (via BUG-005) the MCP key. Container hardening bounds host damage, not this. Documented limitation; exposed/tunnelled it is critical.
repro: POST /api/tools then POST /api/tools/{name}/run with no Authorization header -> 200.
fix: Session login (single user, password from env, secure cookie + CSRF token) for the dashboard; the same bearer or session check on all /api/* routes; keep the bearer for /mcp. Even a simple shared-secret gate on /api/* is a large improvement.

title: JSON-RPC envelope handling is non-conformant: notifications get error replies, batches and malformed bodies get FastAPI 422 before auth
what_happens: Verified: notifications/initialized -> 200 {id:null,error:-32601}; a batch array without auth -> 422 echoing the body; '{not json' -> 422; {id:3} with no method -> -32601 'Method not found: None'. payload: dict means FastAPI parses and rejects before _check_api_key runs.
impact: Every MCP client sends notifications/initialized; spec requires 202 with no body. The TS SDK ignores the stray reply, the Python SDK logs an unknown-id response, strict clients may abort. Unauthenticated callers get validation detail instead of 401.
fix: Take the raw Request, authenticate first, parse manually: -32700 on parse errors, -32600 for non-object/missing method or jsonrpc, 202 empty for messages without id. Or adopt the installed mcp SDK transport (see theme).

title: Successful tools/call results append '[stderr] ...' to the stdout text, breaking JSON output
what_happens: call_tool always folds stderr into the single text item even when isError=false. Verified: a tool printing {"ok": true} plus a DeprecationWarning on stderr returned '{"ok": true}\n[stderr] DeprecationWarning: x' with isError=false.
impact: Any library warning (urllib3, pip/npm notices, DeprecationWarning) makes the documented JSON contract unparseable for clients; tests/test_live_examples.py already works around it.
fix: On success return stdout alone (add structuredContent when it parses as JSON) and put stderr in a separate content item or _meta; fold stderr into text only when isError.

title: Child processes that inherit the pipes turn a successful run into a 'timeout', and the timeout kills only the direct child
what_happens: subprocess.run waits for EOF on stdout/stderr, so a script that starts any background helper (Popen without redirection) blocks until timeout+15 s, is reported exit 124 with stdout discarded, and only the direct child is killed. Backend and security reviewers both observed the grandchild (sleep 37 / a detached writer) surviving after the response.
impact: Orphans accumulate on every call; legitimate scripts that spawn helpers are reported as timeouts; combined with BUG-004 each such run freezes the server for the full 45 s.
repro: Tool: subprocess.Popen(['sleep','37']); print('x') -> returned after timeout as exit 124; pgrep shows sleep still running.
fix: start_new_session=True and os.killpg() on timeout; stop reading pipes shortly after the main process exits; consider prlimit/cgroups.

title: stdout/stderr capture is unbounded and returned in full
what_happens: capture_output=True buffers everything in RAM and the whole text is returned in the HTTP response and the MCP text item. Verified: a 5,000,000-byte stdout came back as a 5,000,074-byte response in 0.06 s; reviewers saw 20 MB pass through.
impact: A runaway print loop can exhaust container memory (killing the service for all clients) or push megabytes into an LLM context, breaking the client conversation.
fix: Stream pipes into bounded buffers (first/last N KB, OMNIFORGE_MAX_OUTPUT_BYTES), mark truncation, kill the group when exceeded.

title: Library list is never re-fetched on navigation: the advertised 412 recovery loops forever and MCP-created or externally deleted tools are invisible
what_happens: loadTools() runs only at startup, after this tab's own writes, on the 'online' event or Retry. activateRoute('tools/edit/NAME') resolves the tool from the in-memory array, so after a 412 the user 'reloads from the library' into the same stale row and gets 412 again on Run, Save, Toggle and Delete. Tools created via omniforge_create_tool never appear; deleted ones stay listed and open a ghost editor.
impact: The main LLM-authoring workflow (ask the assistant to make a tool, then look at it) does not work without a hard reload; the 412 message gives advice that cannot succeed.
fix: Call loadTools() on entering #tools/#overview and before opening #tools/edit/NAME, on visibilitychange/focus, and after a 412/404; offer an explicit 'Reload this tool from server' action; use a page-appropriate 412 message for toggles.

title: Studio cannot create or edit inputSchema: every dashboard-authored tool is parameterless
what_happens: save() reuses the existing schema or {} for new tools; the saved schema is shown read-only with 'Create or change schemas through MCP'. {} is stored as EMPTY_SCHEMA with additionalProperties:false, so any argument an LLM passes is rejected.
impact: A browser-made tool can never take inputs unless an LLM or an API client created it; the README documents this but it undermines the core 'write a script, publish it as a tool' promise.
repro: Create a tool in the studio, then tools/call it with any argument -> 'Arguments do not match inputSchema'.
fix: Schema builder (name/type/required/description rows) plus raw-JSON mode validated by validate_schema; revision-guarded like code.

title: MCP bearer key is equivalent to a shell: omniforge_create_tool makes an active tool with no approval step
what_happens: save_tool runs with is_active defaulting to true; the new tool is callable on the next tools/call. The security reviewer created a tool over /mcp and read the server's own key back with it.
impact: A prompt-injected model, or any client given the key, obtains in-container RCE and self-leaks the key. Single-user LAN: medium; exposed: critical.
fix: Default MCP-created tools to disabled with a dashboard approval, or scope keys (author vs call); never expose the key to scripts (BUG-005).

title: Non-UTF-8 script output discards the real stdout and exit code
what_happens: subprocess.run(text=True) decodes strictly; a UnicodeDecodeError is caught by the generic except and replaced with stdout='' and exit 1. Verified: b'result ok \xff' + exit 3 -> {stdout:'', stderr:"'utf-8' codec can't decode ...", exit_code:1}. The scratch file and the template are also opened without an explicit encoding (locale-dependent outside the image).
impact: Tools that print Latin-1 data or binary lose their output and status; users debug a codec message instead of their script.
fix: Capture bytes and decode with errors='replace' (or encoding='utf-8', errors='replace'); open files with encoding='utf-8'.

title: All tools share one cwd that is also sys.path[0]; scratch scripts are never removed
what_happens: Verified: cwd and sys.path[0] are both SCRATCH_ROOT and other tools' <id>.py files are visible there. Any module or data file one tool writes (helpers.py, json.py, package.json with type:module) is imported or honoured by every other tool; deleted tools' source stays on disk.
impact: Silent cross-tool breakage and shadowing; stale copies of deleted code; with BUG-004 fixed, concurrent runs of one tool would rewrite the same path.
repro: rr/checks.py check R; listing of the scratch dir after deletes.
fix: Per-run tempfile.TemporaryDirectory under SCRATCH_ROOT as cwd, removed afterwards; run Python with -P (3.11+) so the script dir is not on sys.path.

title: Legacy duplicate-name rows are advertised twice in tools/list and cannot be deleted from the dashboard
what_happens: Mechanism verified by inserting two 'rr_dup' rows: tools/list listed the name twice; DELETE with If-Match set to either revision -> 412 both times (database.delete demands exactly one row). The pre-28161d0 POST created a new id on every save with no duplicate check, so such rows can exist in David's DB; whether they do is unverified.
impact: LLM APIs reject tool lists with duplicate names, so every chat loading the server fails; the dashboard offers no way out.
fix: De-duplicate in MCPHandler.tools() (newest wins, log a warning); match If-Match against the row with that revision and delete by id; startup report of duplicates; add a UNIQUE index after a one-off migration.

title: Cross-tool dependency-cache poisoning via the writable, script-reachable OMNIFORGE_LIB_ROOT
what_happens: Scripts run as the uid that owns the cache and learn its path from the inherited env. A script (or a malicious dependency) can plant a module and a .complete marker in another tool's cache, which that tool then imports via PYTHONPATH/NODE_PATH. Security reviewer wrote into the lib root from a tool.
impact: One compromised tool or package silently and persistently compromises every other tool across restarts. The README documents that scripts can write other tools' caches, so this extends a known limitation into persistence.
fix: Keep the lib root out of the script env (BUG-005); copy or bind the needed cache read-only per run, or install under a different uid.

title: Empty OMNIFORGE_API_KEY silently disables MCP auth while the image binds 0.0.0.0
what_happens: if not API_KEY: return True. The public image, the README compose and docker-compose.yml default the key to empty; .env.example ships 'change-me'. David's instance has the key set, so this is not triggered locally.
impact: Anyone who runs dbzocchi/omniforge:latest without setting the key has a fully open RCE service on their network. Real deployment: not affected; keyless from the public image: critical.
repro: Start without OMNIFORGE_API_KEY; POST /mcp with no Authorization -> 200.
fix: Fail closed: refuse to start (or bind 127.0.0.1 only) when the key is empty unless OMNIFORGE_ALLOW_NO_AUTH=1; log loudly.

title: Catastrophic regex in a tool's inputSchema 'pattern' blocks the event loop on every call (ReDoS)
what_happens: validate_arguments runs jsonschema with Python's backtracking re on the event loop. Verified: pattern '^(a+)+$' with a 27-character argument took 4.38 s and a concurrent GET /api/config waited 3.88 s; cost doubles per extra character (35 chars = roughly 20 minutes).
impact: A mistaken or malicious schema (settable by any API/MCP client) hangs the whole server for as long as desired; unlike a script, the timeout does not apply.
fix: Validate arguments off the loop with a hard time limit, or use the `regex` module with a timeout; reject nested-quantifier patterns on save.

title: PUT /api/tools/{name} silently re-enables a disabled tool and wipes its input schema when fields are omitted
what_happens: PUT reuses ToolIn, whose is_active defaults to true and json_schema to {}. Verified: a disabled tool with a schema updated with only {name, code} became enabled with EMPTY_SCHEMA. The dashboard sends every field and is unaffected.
impact: API scripts and LLM-driven edits republish disabled tools and break callers that pass arguments.
fix: Separate update model that defaults omitted fields to the stored values (model_fields_set), or require all fields on PUT.

title: Timeout accounting: exit code 124 is reported as a timeout, the message states the configured limit not the effective one, and partial output is discarded
what_happens: timed_out = (exit_code == 124). Verified: sys.exit(124) after print -> timed_out:true in 10 ms; MCP text 'done\n[exit 124]\n[timeout]'. On a real timeout stderr says 'exceeded 30000ms' although 45 s elapsed, and TimeoutExpired.stdout is thrown away.
impact: Users chase a non-existent server timeout (GNU timeout wrappers exit 124); hang diagnosis loses the progress output.
fix: Set timed_out in the TimeoutExpired branch; report MAX_TIMEOUT_MS + grace in the message; keep exc.stdout/stderr decoded leniently.

title: Dependency cache hygiene: crashed installs leave .install-* staging trees, and old digests and deleted tools' caches are never pruned
what_happens: The finally: rmtree(staging) cannot run if the process is killed mid-install (backend reviewer verified a leftover .install-* after SIGKILL). Nothing ever removes a superseded <requirements-hash> directory or the <tool-id-hash> tree of a deleted tool.
impact: Steady disk growth in the persistent omniforge_lib volume on the NAS (Node trees can be hundreds of MB each).
repro: SIGKILL during a real install; change a tool's requirements twice and list OMNIFORGE_LIB_ROOT.
fix: While holding the digest lock, sweep stale .install-* siblings; on tool delete or requirements change, remove unreferenced digests; optional startup sweep with a size report.

title: OMNIFORGE_MAX_SCRIPT_MEMORY_MB is declared but never enforced; no rlimits on scripts
what_happens: MAX_MEMORY_MB is read and unused; /proc/self/limits inside a tool shows unlimited address space, RSS, CPU and processes.
impact: A tool can exhaust the container's memory or fork-bomb it; Docker --memory/--pids-limit (recommended in the README) bounds the container, not one script.
fix: preexec_fn applying RLIMIT_AS, RLIMIT_NPROC, RLIMIT_CPU, RLIMIT_FSIZE; document that the setting is now enforced.

title: initialize echoes any protocolVersion (even empty), ping returns null, unknown tools are not protocol errors
what_happens: Verified: protocolVersion '1999-01-01' echoed back; ping -> result:null (spec: {}); tools/call of an unknown name -> isError result instead of -32602.
impact: Clients believe unsupported versions are supported; SDK clients validating ping as an object treat it as failed.
fix: Keep a SUPPORTED_VERSIONS list and negotiate; return {} for ping; -32602 for unknown tool names.

title: GET /mcp is an unauthenticated SSE stub that emits a made-up event and closes
what_happens: Verified: GET /mcp with no key -> 200 text/event-stream 'event: initial-connections' then EOF. The spec expects 405 when no stream is offered.
impact: Inconsistent auth model; Streamable HTTP clients may treat the closed stream as a dropped connection. Disclosure is negligible.
fix: Return 405 with Allow: POST after the auth check until a real stream exists (the SDK transport provides one).

title: REST 422 responses echo submitted code and arguments
what_happens: FastAPI's default RequestValidationError handler returns detail[].input. Verified: a code value containing NUL and a batch body to /mcp were echoed back. The MCP path deliberately strips inputs (include_input=False).
impact: Scripts and test arguments containing credentials end up in error bodies, HAR captures and proxy logs.
fix: Register a RequestValidationError handler returning only loc and msg.

title: Release hygiene: unpinned and undeclared dependencies, :latest pushed without tests, compose/image drift, no health endpoint, HEAD 405
what_happens: jsonschema and referencing are imported but arrive only via the unused mcp package; nothing is pinned; dockerhub.yml pushes dbzocchi/omniforge:latest on every main push while test.yml excludes main; docker-compose.yml names ionic-developer/omniforge:latest and sets unused OMNIFORGE_RUNTIME_IMAGE/scripts volume; no /healthz or HEALTHCHECK; HEAD / -> 405 (verified).
impact: A dependency release can publish a broken :latest with no test gate; Unraid cannot tell a wedged loop from healthy.
fix: Declare and pin dependencies (lock file, Dependabot); run the suites in dockerhub.yml before pushing; align the compose image; add /healthz + HEALTHCHECK.

title: Tab/Shift+Tab indentation uses setRangeText, which wipes the editor's undo history
what_happens: Programmatic value changes clear the textarea undo stack in Chromium. Frontend reviewer verified: type, Tab, Ctrl+Z twice -> nothing undone.
impact: Work loss after the most common editing key in a code editor.
fix: Use document.execCommand('insertText') after setting the selection, falling back to setRangeText when it returns false.

title: Connect 'HTTP request template' omits Content-Type: application/json
what_happens: Verified on the running instance: the template's headers contain only Authorization. curl -d defaults to form encoding, so copying it yields a 422 'Input should be a valid dictionary'.
impact: The one connection recipe the product offers fails when followed literally.
repro: Open #connect; copy the template into curl.
fix: Add Content-Type and Accept to the template and provide a ready-to-paste curl and client config.

title: Tool-name pattern attribute is an invalid v-flag regex: client-side validation is silently disabled
what_happens: Verified in Chrome 155: console error 'Pattern attribute value ... is not a valid regular expression ... /v: Invalid character in character class'; '1 bad name!' -> patternMismatch false, checkValidity true. The server still rejects (422) but #nameError/aria-invalid never fire.
impact: Keyboard and screen-reader users get only a toast; the pattern error appears on every editor load.
fix: pattern="[a-zA-Z][a-zA-Z0-9_\-]{0,62}" and map 422 name errors to #nameError like the 409 path.

title: Validation feedback in the studio is generic or hidden: schema errors give no path, package errors leave the Packages section collapsed
what_happens: validate_arguments raises 'Arguments do not match inputSchema' with no property or keyword; requirement errors arrive as a toast while #advancedSettings stays closed and the textarea is not marked invalid.
impact: First-time users cannot tell which input or package line is wrong.
repro: Run a tool with required inputs using {}.
fix: Return value-free locations (path + keyword); open the disclosure and set aria-invalid on error.

title: Copy buttons never work on the plain-HTTP LAN origin the real deployment uses
what_happens: copyText relies solely on navigator.clipboard, which is undefined outside secure contexts. Verified by loading http://172.24.1.37:18307/#connect: isSecureContext=false, navigator.clipboard absent, clicking Copy shows the error toast 'Clipboard access is unavailable'.
impact: On http://192.168.0.180:8000 both Copy buttons always fail; the same insecure context also means no service worker, no offline page and no Install button (documented).
repro: Open the dashboard via a non-localhost http:// origin and click Copy.
fix: Fall back to a temporary textarea + document.execCommand('copy'), or select the text and tell the user; mention HTTP in the hint.

title: Tools saved by earlier versions with non-object schemas become unrunnable and unsaveable from the dashboard
what_happens: Mechanism verified by inserting a row with json_schema_json {"properties":{...}}: tools/list still advertises it, MCP call and /run return 'inputSchema must declare type object', and a dashboard-shaped PUT (which always carries the stored schema) returns 422. The pre-28161d0 API stored any supplied schema verbatim, but the old dashboard had no schema field, so such rows exist only if a client posted one.
impact: If present, the tool is stuck until repaired by a hand-crafted API PUT.
fix: Normalise or flag legacy schemas on read/startup; let the dashboard reset a schema.

title: Installer PATH is hard-coded, so npm is not found outside the Docker image layout
what_happens: _installer_environment fixes PATH and npm is looked up only there; in WSL two unit tests error with 'npm runtime is unavailable'.
impact: Node tools with requirements fail on any non-image layout; the test suite cannot run outside the container.
fix: Derive npm from the resolved node binary's directory and prepend it; mock npm discovery in tests.

title: Requirement validation accepts archive filenames and rejects canonical .postN/.devN pins
what_happens: Verified with validate_requirements: ACCEPT foo.tar.gz, foo.whl (python), foo.tgz (node); REJECT pkg==1.0.post1; ACCEPT pkg==1.0post1.
impact: Confusing installer errors for archive-looking names; valid pins rejected.
fix: Reject .whl/.zip/.tar.gz/.tgz/.tar suffixes; allow an optional '.' before post/dev, or parse with packaging.

title: Dependency cache key ignores the interpreter and Node version
what_happens: The digest covers only the requirements list; caches persist in the volume across image upgrades.
impact: After a Python or Node major bump, compiled packages fail at import with no reinstall trigger.
fix: Include sys.implementation.cache_tag / node major in the directory name.

title: API key comparison is not constant-time; the raw key is accepted without the Bearer scheme; 401 lacks WWW-Authenticate
what_happens: Verified: 'Authorization: test-key' -> 200; 401 has no WWW-Authenticate header; token == API_KEY.
impact: Timing side channel is impractical on a LAN; the bare-value acceptance is a hygiene issue.
fix: Require Bearer, hmac.compare_digest, add WWW-Authenticate: Bearer.

title: MCP tools/call executes from the 5-second process cache while dashboard runs read fresh rows; PUT without If-Match can resurrect a deleted id
what_happens: call_tool resolves from db.get_tool_list() (cached) whereas api_run_tool uses get_tool(fresh=True); api_update_tool reads 'existing' from the cache and upserts ON CONFLICT(id).
impact: Only observable with more than one worker or out-of-process DB edits (neither used today).
repro: Backend reviewer: edit SQLite directly, MCP returned old code for up to 5 s.
fix: Fetch the single row fresh in tools/call; use fresh reads in update; fail the upsert when the id is gone.

title: No size limits on code, description, schema or request bodies, and no rate limiting (slowapi installed but unused)
what_happens: Security reviewer stored an ~8 MiB code field; no maxLength on ToolIn/CREATE_SCHEMA; nothing throttles /mcp or /run.
impact: A multi-megabyte description ends up in every tools/list; brute force of the key is unthrottled if exposed.
repro: POST /api/tools with a large code field.
fix: maxLength on fields, a body-size limit, and wire slowapi or a reverse-proxy limit.

title: No security headers on the dashboard (CSP, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, nosniff on HTML)
what_happens: Verified: GET / returns only cache-control: no-store.
impact: Clickjacking is possible; any future XSS would be unmitigated. No XSS sink exists today.
fix: Add a nonce-based CSP, X-Frame-Options: DENY, Referrer-Policy: no-referrer, X-Content-Type-Options.

title: Node runtime in the image comes unpinned from Debian apt and is an end-of-life line
what_happens: apt-get install nodejs npm on whatever Debian release python:3.12-slim currently resolves to: Node 18 on bookworm (EOL April 2025) or Node 20 on trixie (EOL April 2026). Not verified against the published image.
impact: Modern packages increasingly require Node 20/22; no security fixes for the runtime that executes tool code.
fix: Install a pinned, supported Node (NodeSource or official tarball) and record the version in the README.

title: After a deploy the new dashboard HTML is rendered with the old cached CSS/fonts until 'Update available' is accepted
what_happens: Assets are served cache-first by the old worker while the new one waits; nothing ties the cache name to asset content. Frontend reviewer verified on a scratch copy. Only applies in secure contexts; on the plain-HTTP LAN deployment the worker never registers.
impact: Not triggered on the real deployment; medium if served over HTTPS.
fix: Version asset URLs with a content hash emitted by the HTML, or serve assets network-first.

title: Test inputs and displayed output are round-tripped through JS numbers
what_happens: JSON.parse/JSON.stringify of inputs and stdout: integers above 2^53 change, 1.0 becomes 1, duplicate keys collapse.
impact: Tests with 64-bit ids act on a different record; the output panel differs from what MCP clients receive (though JS-based clients share the limitation).
fix: Send the raw textarea text; show stdout verbatim with an optional pretty toggle.

title: 'Update available' stays visible and does nothing in other tabs after the update is accepted elsewhere
what_happens: No controllerchange listener outside the click handler; SKIP_WAITING to an already-active worker is a no-op. Secure contexts only.
impact: Confusing dead button; not triggered on plain HTTP.
repro: Two tabs on the HTTPS scratch copy.
fix: Listen for controllerchange in every tab and check waitingWorker.state.

title: Offline fallback says 'Your workspace is online.' and ignores dark mode
what_happens: The headline contradicts 'Connection needed'; product.css has no prefers-color-scheme rules and the page sets no data-theme. Secure contexts only.
impact: Cosmetic; not reachable on plain HTTP.
repro: Go offline on the HTTPS copy.
fix: Reword; add prefers-color-scheme overrides or an inline theme script.

title: Connection indicator dot is always accent-coloured; Ctrl+S offline gives no feedback
what_happens: .connection:before uses var(--accent) regardless of state; save() returns silently when offline.
impact: Only the text changes; users are unsure whether a save happened.
fix: data-state on #connectionState with warn/danger colours; notify on offline save attempts.

title: Enable/disable switch's accessible name is the action, contradicting its state
what_happens: aria-label 'Disable X' with aria-checked=true reads as 'Disable X, switch, on'.
impact: Screen-reader users cannot tell the state.
fix: Stable label 'Enabled for AI: X' and let aria-checked carry the state.

title: 'Escape, then Shift+Tab' does not leave the code editor and unindents the line instead
what_happens: The Shift keydown (key 'Shift') clears leaveEditor before the Tab arrives.
impact: Keyboard users are trapped and their code is modified.
fix: Ignore pure modifier keys when resetting the flag.

title: Scrollable output and request-template regions are not focusable (axe scrollable-region-focusable)
what_happens: #out pre and #requestTemplate have max-height/overflow but no tabindex (#savedInputSchema has one).
impact: Keyboard/switch users in Safari cannot scroll long output.
fix: tabindex=0 plus aria-label on both.

title: viewport-fit=cover without left/right safe-area padding in phone landscape
what_happens: Only safe-area-inset-bottom is handled; the desktop rail layout applies above 640 px wide.
impact: Rail under the notch on notched phones in landscape; not rendered in the review.
fix: padding-left: max(12px, env(safe-area-inset-left)) on .rail and matching right padding.

title: Cancelling a dirty Back navigation overwrites the previous history entry
what_happens: hashchange handler calls history.replaceState on the entry the user went back to, replacing #tools with the editor route.
impact: The next Back skips Tools and may land on a stale editor.
fix: pushState the editor route (or history.go(1)) instead of replaceState.

title: Every keystroke rebuilds the whole line-number gutter
what_happens: updateGutter splits the whole script and rebuilds the gutter string on each input; 20k lines -> ~90 ms per keystroke.
impact: Typing lags on large pasted scripts.
fix: Only append/trim gutter lines when the count changes.

title: At 320 px the editor footer squeezes 'Run / Test' onto three lines
what_happens: Footer buttons get flex:1 with no nowrap and no wrapping of .actions.
impact: Looks broken on the smallest phones.
fix: white-space: nowrap and flex-wrap, or stack full-width below 360 px.
